'''''Pterocarya fraxinifolia'''''  is a species of [[tree]] in the [[Juglandaceae]] family.  It is commonly known as the '''Caucasian wingnut''' or '''Caucasian walnut'''.  It is native to the Caucasian region [[Armenia]], [[Azerbaijan]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], [[Iran]], [[Russia]], [[Ukraine]]  and  [[Turkey]]. It was introduced to [[France]] in 1784, and to [[Great Britain]] after 1800.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.keele.ac.uk/arboretum/trees/speciesaccounts/caucasianwing-nut/|title=Caucasian Wingnut – Keele University Arboretum|access-date=2010-10-21}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Pterocarya fraxinifolia JPG3a.jpg|left|thumb|Caucasian wingnut tree]]
The tree is [[monoecious]] and grows to a height of < 30 m, the short, thick [[Trunk (botany)|bole]] supporting widely spreading branches to form a rounded structure, not unlike the [[Ulmus glabra|wych elm]].  The [[leaf shape|pinnate]] leaves can exceed 60 cm in length, comprising 7 - 27 [[sessility (botany)|sessile]] leaflets. The flowers appear in April, the male catkins thick and green, 7.5 – 12.5 cm long, the females longer with less dense flowers, bearing red [[style (botany)|style]]s forming fruiting catkins 30 – 50 cm long, the green, winged, nuts approximately 1.8 cm wide.<ref name=Phillips>Phillips, R. (1978). ''Trees in Britain, Europe & North America''. Pan Books, London.</ref>

==Ecology==
The species is fast growing and grows best on flat ground or shallow slopes near river banks and in deep moist soils. The climate associated with the distribution of this tree includes mild winters and mild humid summers. It generally grows in mixed stands with other species and rarely grows in pure stands.{{cn|date=March 2021}}

==Fossil record==
Fossils of ''Pterocarya fraxinifolia'' have been described from the [[fossil flora of Kızılcahamam district]] in [[Turkey]], which is of early [[Pliocene]] age.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kasaplıgil |first1=Baki |title=Ankara, Kızılcahamam yakınındaki Güvem köyü civarında bulunan son tersiyer kozalaklı-yeşil yapraklı ormanı |journal=Bulletin of the Mineral Research and Exploration |date=1977 |volume=88 |page=94-102 |url=https://dergipark.org.tr/en/pub/bulletinofmre/issue/3914/52153 |publisher=[[General Directorate of Mineral Research and Exploration (Turkey)|General Directorate of Mineral Research and Exploration]] |location=Ankara |language=tr, en |format=PDF |trans-title=A Late-Tertiary Conifer-Hardwood Forest From the Vicinity of Güvem Village, Near Kızılcahamam, Ankara}}</ref>
